rulings.challenge_claim: Two challenges land here: that the cut before verse 5 separates the complaint from the reply it draws at a join carrying no tier-1 device, with a treachery catchword straddling that seam undisclosed; and that the opening warrant's new-first-person-voice reading is contradicted by dispute, testing and kidneys vocabulary tying 12:1-3 back across the opening seam to 11:20, likewise undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Distinct defects at opposite edges of one row; both are real, and one framing needs correction. Opening edge: 11:18-20 is already first-person prophetic speech -- הֽוֹדִיעַ֖נִי וָֽאֵדָ֑עָה at oshb:Jer.11.18 (byte) and גִּלִּ֥יתִי אֶת רִיבִֽי at oshb:Jer.11.20 (byte) -- so the first person at 12:1 RESUMES across the intervening koh-amar reply rather than opening a new voice, and the warrant as written is byte-false. The ties verify on their named objects, not merely their digits: אָרִ֖יב at oshb:Jer.12.1 (byte; that form, sweep: 2 verses) answers רִיבִֽי at oshb:Jer.11.20 (byte; sweep: 3 verses); the kidneys token stands at בֹּחֵ֥ן כְּלָי֖וֹת וָלֵ֑ב in oshb:Jer.11.20 and at מִכִּלְיוֹתֵיהֶֽם in oshb:Jer.12.2 (both byte; that token, sweep: 4 verses); and וּבָחַנְתָּ֥ לִבִּ֖י at oshb:Jer.12.3 (byte; sweep: 3 verses) answers the testing participle of oshb:Jer.11.20 (sweep: 3 verses). Closing edge: 12:5 opens כִּ֣י אֶת רַגְלִ֥ים רַ֨צְתָּה֙ וַיַּלְא֔וּךָ (byte) with no messenger, attribution or word-event formula, and the nearest koh-amar-YHWH sites are 11:22 before and 12:14 after (sweep: 152 verses), none between; כָּל בֹּ֥גְדֵי בָֽגֶד closes oshb:Jer.12.1 while בָּ֣גְדוּ בָ֔ךְ stands in oshb:Jer.12.6 (both byte), the family's only two sites in chapters 10-13 (bare consonantal substring, sweep: 12 verses) -- a byte-true catchword crossing this row's own closing seam, undisclosed. Three corrections to the closing-seam framing: an argument resting on the ABSENCE of a paragraph mark at the verse-4/5 join is barred, that layer being tier-3 in the Prophets with absence never counterevidence; the marks do not merely flank the proposed six-verse exchange, since a setumah stands at MT 12:3 inside it (single-witness, tier-3, and the row does disclose it); and כָּל בֹּ֥גְדֵי בָֽגֶד is verse-final at 12:1, not the complaint's opening. The cut itself survives on ground the row never argues: 12:1-4 names its addressee, צַדִּ֤יק אַתָּה֙ יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.12.1, byte), while 12:5-6 addresses the one whose brothers and father's house are in view -- a byte-visible addressee-referent shift, which is a ruled seam class.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the new-first-person-voice wording with the byte-shown resumption of the first-person voice standing at 11:18-20 across the koh-amar reply of 11:21-23, and ground the cut before verse 5 on the addressee-referent shift read off the pointed bytes (YHWH named as addressee in 12:1-4; the prophet's own brothers and father's house as addressee in 12:5-6) rather than on the absence of a formula. device_notes: disclose BOTH straddling device sets with swept object and verse count -- the dispute, testing and kidneys ties running back to 11:20, and the treachery catchword running forward to 12:6. Delete any sentence resting on a paragraph mark being absent. Boundary PROPOSAL (boss adoption required; not author work): merge 12:1-6 into one petition-and-reply row. Test the cure must pass: the warrant states each half's addressee from the pointed bytes; every device straddling either of the row's own seams is disclosed with object and count; and no evidentiary sentence rests on marker absence.

rulings.challenge_claim: That the opening cut at verse 5 is the same unmarked join challenged from the complaint's side; and that a treachery catchword crosses that seam undisclosed while both Hebrew splices in the warrant are paired with English running past the spliced extent, the verse's single count-only seg also going undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: The seam arm is the same defect adjudicated at the complaint's side, not a second finding; the gloss-parity arm is distinct and lands on its own. Parity break one: the splice ends at וַיַּלְא֔וּךָ (oshb:Jer.12.5, byte) while the paired English runs on through the horses clause, which renders תְּתַֽחֲרֶ֖ה אֶת הַסּוּסִ֑ים (oshb:Jer.12.5, byte) outside the splice. Parity break two: the splice אַל תַּאֲמֵ֣ן בָּ֔ם (oshb:Jer.12.6, byte) is paired with English running on through the beautiful-words clause, which renders כִּֽי יְדַבְּר֥וּ אֵלֶ֖יךָ טוֹבֽוֹת (oshb:Jer.12.6, byte) outside it. Gloss extent must equal splice extent, and neither pairing meets that. Catchword: בָּ֣גְדוּ בָ֔ךְ in oshb:Jer.12.6 answers the verse-final כָּל בֹּ֥גְדֵי בָֽגֶד of oshb:Jer.12.1 (both byte) across this row's opening seam -- the family's only two sites in chapters 10-13 (bare consonantal substring, sweep: 12 verses) -- undisclosed. The count-only seg layer does carry one seg at MT 12:5, but that layer is count-only with no intra-verse position and sits outside the unconditional paragraph-mark symmetry arm, so its omission is a completeness point of low weight and does not lift severity. The high severity attached to the unmarked seam is not sustained: device_notes already concedes that no formula marks the turn, the row holds at reduced confidence with the frontier flag raised -- the sanctioned honest hold -- and the seam survives on the addressee-referent shift visible in the bytes.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: re-cut both pairings so each curly-quoted English run renders exactly its adjacent splice -- either extend the splice at oshb:Jer.12.5 through the horses clause and the splice at oshb:Jer.12.6 through the beautiful-words clause, or trim each English run back to the spliced clause; each pairing is one edit. device_notes: disclose the treachery catchword crossing the row's opening seam with its swept object and verse count, and record the single count-only seg at oshb:Jer.12.5 as single-witness with no position claim. Test the cure must pass: every curly-quoted WEB run in the field renders exactly the Hebrew spliced beside it and nothing more, checked against both witnesses' bytes at the same verse; and every byte-true device straddling the row's own seams is disclosed.

rulings.challenge_claim: That the one-unit warrant's claim that no addressee change and no discourse imperative interrupts 12:7-13 is falsified by the span's own bytes at two verses -- the plural imperatives of 12:9 and the second-person plural suffix at 12:13.
rulings.grounds: The defect is real; one arm of its framing is not. Byte-true: oshb:Jer.12.9 carries לְכ֗וּ אִסְפ֛וּ together with הֵתָ֥יוּ (byte; that imperative pair, sweep: 1 verse), so an unqualified denial that any discourse imperative interrupts the span is false at the token level, and the feature goes undisclosed. Byte-true: וּבֹ֨שׁוּ֙ מִתְּבוּאֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם at oshb:Jer.12.13 (byte) carries a second-person masculine plural suffix and turns the speech to the addressed people, a party other than the summoned agents of 12:9 -- likewise undisclosed, and it does contradict the no-addressee-change arm as written. Byte-false: calling 12:13 the span's FIRST direct second-person address does not hold, since the 12:9 imperatives are themselves second-person forms standing four verses earlier; an ordinal of that kind needs its own digit-bearing sweep of the named object and does not survive one. The koh-amar arm holds: nearest sites are 11:22 before and 12:14 after (sweep: 152 verses), none between. The one-unit result also survives: the 12:9 imperatives summon the field's creatures inside the poem's own imagery rather than opening a fresh commission to an audience -- the class this row treats as a seam at 13:15 and 13:18 -- and 12:13 carries no fresh discourse frame. What fails is the unqualified wording and the missing disclosure, not the boundary.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the unqualified three-part denial with a qualified statement naming both in-span features and why neither is a seam of the ruled classes -- the plural imperatives at 12:9 summoning agents inside the poem's imagery, and the second-person plural suffix at 12:13 turning to the addressed people without a fresh discourse frame; keep the koh-amar arm, which the census supports. device_notes: disclose both features with swept object and verse count. Test the cure must pass: no absolute absence claim stands where the span's own bytes carry a token of the named class, and any first/only/sole ordinal carries an adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming the swept object and unit.

rulings.challenge_claim: That both frame warrants pair a byte-tier Hebrew splice with English rendering different words of the same verse, so neither the onset formula nor the closure formula is glossed by the text offered as its match; and that the verse's single count-only seg is undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Both pairings are broken on the bytes. At 12:14 the other witness renders the formula verse-initially as “Yahweh says,” (web:Jer.12.14), while the spliced כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.12.14, byte) is paired with the plucking-up clause, which renders הִנְנִ֤י נֹֽתְשָׁם֙ מֵעַ֣ל אַדְמָתָ֔ם (oshb:Jer.12.14, byte) -- a different stretch of the same verse. At 12:17 the other witness renders the formula verse-finally as “says Yahweh.” (web:Jer.12.17), while the spliced נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.12.17, byte) is paired with the clause preceding it and that English omits the formula's own rendering altogether, inverting the pairing. Gloss extent must equal splice extent; neither pairing meets it. The substantive reading survives: נְאֻם יְהוָֽה is verse-final at oshb:Jer.12.17 (byte), and a fresh private commission opens at oshb:Jer.13.1 with כֹּֽה אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י (byte; that shape, sweep: 3 verses), so the closure corroboration is correctly placed under the closure-only handling this formula carries at its book-wide density. The count-only seg at MT 12:14 is inventory-true but position-free and outside the unconditional paragraph-mark symmetry arm -- a low-weight completeness point that does not lift severity.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: re-pair both matches -- pair the koh-amar splice with the WEB rendering “Yahweh says,” (web:Jer.12.14) and the neum splice with “says Yahweh.” (web:Jer.12.17); if the plucking-up English is retained, splice the clause it renders beside it. device_notes: record the single count-only seg at oshb:Jer.12.14 as single-witness with no position claim. Test the cure must pass: each curly-quoted WEB run renders exactly the Hebrew spliced beside it, verified against both witnesses' bytes at the same verse, with the formula's own rendering never omitted from the pairing that carries it.

rulings.challenge_claim: That the no-scene-shift clause is contested by an explicit temporal frame and a separate divine-speech onset at 13:6 the enumeration passes over, that the 13:1 formula carries a form label the pointed bytes do not support, and that 13:3's onset is asserted without a pointed splice while 13:8's is spliced.
rulings.grounds: All three arms hold, at low weight. oshb:Jer.13.6 opens וַיְהִ֕י מִקֵּ֖ץ יָמִ֣ים רַבִּ֑ים and then carries the separate divine-speech onset וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י (both byte), commanding a second journey to the river -- an explicit time-and-place transition standing inside the span, so the clause that no addressee or scene shift interrupts the sequence overstates what the bytes carry. The form label fails on the bytes: אָמַ֨ר at oshb:Jer.13.1 (byte) is a suffix-conjugation form, while the narrative wayyiqtol shapes of this span stand at 13:3, 13:6, 13:7 and 13:8 -- so the narrative-preterite label is a form-class claim the pointed text does not carry, and no morphology layer is staged that could rescue it (the challenge's own account of where the wayyiqtol shape stands is narrower than the span's bytes). The commission reading it reaches for is nevertheless corroborated: כֹּֽה אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י stands at 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses), distinguishing it from the public-oracle onsets. The splice asymmetry is real: the word-event at 13:8 is spliced at byte tier while the equally load-bearing onset at 13:3 is carried on the other witness's rendering alone. The one-unit result stands unchanged: the addressee never changes across 13:1-11, and the command, performance and interpretation phases of one enacted sign hold together absent an intervening seam of the ruled classes.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: qualify the scene clause -- name the time-and-place transition at 13:6 and state why it opens no ruled seam (same addressee, same enacted sign, no fresh commission to a new audience); replace the narrative-preterite label with a description the bytes support, namely the koh-amar shape standing in a private commission to the prophet rather than a public oracle onset, with its 3-verse book-wide sweep cited beside it; splice the word-event at oshb:Jer.13.3 at byte tier with its ref and tier named, matching the treatment of 13:8. Test the cure must pass: every form-class label is readable off the pointed bytes cited beside it, and every load-bearing device claim carries its own splice at a named tier.

rulings.challenge_claim: That the form made to carry the opening seam recurs byte-identically one verse later inside the span, that its imperative label is not what the pointed bytes show, and that the closure warrant places a formula it never splices at a position the bytes contradict.
rulings.grounds: Two arms hold as stated; one sub-claim needs correction. Recurrence: וְאָמַרְתָּ֨ אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם opens oshb:Jer.13.12 and the identical pointed run opens oshb:Jer.13.13 (both byte; that run at byte tier, sweep: 4 verses; the same shape at the consonantal tier, sweep: 18 verses), so the marker carrying the seam is not seam-exclusive and the in-span recurrence is undisclosed. That refines rather than kills the seam: what separates 13:12 from the belt's interpretation is a fresh commissioned saying to a broad audience after that interpretation closes, and the recurrence at 13:13 continues the same commissioned speech rather than opening a second unit. Form label: וְאָמַרְתָּ֨ אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם is a waw-prefixed suffix-conjugation form, not a morphological imperative -- the imperatives in the neighbourhood are שִׁמְע֥וּ וְהַאֲזִ֖ינוּ at oshb:Jer.13.15, תְּנוּ֩ at oshb:Jer.13.16 and אֱמֹ֥ר לַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְלַגְּבִירָ֖ה at oshb:Jer.13.18 (all byte) -- so the label is a byte-checkable claim the text does not carry, though the clause does function as a commissioning frame. Closure position: at oshb:Jer.13.14 the formula נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה stands at the athnach with לֹֽא אֶחְמ֧וֹל and two further negated clauses running to the verse-final מֵהַשְׁחִיתָֽם (byte), so describing it as marking the unit's end misplaces it inside its verse; the closure reading itself survives, a fresh onset following at oshb:Jer.13.15 (sweep: 1 verse). Correction: the paragraph mark is NOT at the internal repetition point -- it is keyed to MT 13:12 while the repetition stands at 13:13; the row's paragraph disclosure for this span is complete and correctly typed (setumah at MT 13:12 and MT 13:14, single-witness, tier-3), and no variant note falls inside 13:12-13:14. The same misplacement of the closing formula is reproduced in the account that supports this row.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: describe the opening as a waw-prefixed suffix-conjugation commissioning clause rather than an imperative, and disclose that the identical pointed run opens 13:13 inside the span (with its byte-tier verse count), stating why the recurrence continues the commissioned speech instead of opening a second unit; restate the closure as the formula standing inside 13:14 with further clauses following it, corroborated by the fresh imperative onset at 13:15, not as a formula standing at the unit's end, and splice it at byte tier where it is asserted. If the re-description changes the driver, observed_substrate_signals, strongest_rejected_alternative, unit_type and confidence re-open with it. Test the cure must pass: no form-class label stands that the pointed bytes contradict; any marker made to carry a seam is swept for in-span recurrence with the recurrence disclosed; and any position claim about a formula is read off that verse's own pointed bytes.

rulings.challenge_claim: That a variant note at 13:16 inside the span goes undisclosed even though the disclosure layer is engaged for the paragraph marks, and that a flock lexeme attested in 6 verses book-wide crosses the closing seam undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Both hold. oshb:Jer.13.16 stands inside the span and carries one note in the single-witness variant inventory; it is visible in the verse's own bytes as the unpointed ketiv ישית beside its pointed qere וְשִׁ֖ית (byte). The row's disclosure reaches only the paragraph marks at MT 13:14 and MT 13:17, so the disclosure set is incomplete on the book's largest single-witness variant layer at a verse inside the row's own span. Cohesion: עֵ֥דֶר יְהוָֽה closes oshb:Jer.13.17, the row's own last verse, and the same lexeme returns as הָעֵ֨דֶר֙ at oshb:Jer.13.20 (both byte; that consonantal form, sweep: 6 verses) -- a byte-true tie crossing this row's closing seam, undisclosed, arguing continuity against the cut until it is disclosed. The onset is sound and verified: שִׁמְע֥וּ וְהַאֲזִ֖ינוּ re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Jer.13.15 and that imperative pair is unique in the book (sweep: 1 verse). The third arm is minor but right: declining the lament typing by appeal to which spans are enumerated is not a byte ground; the ground that does hold is וְאִם֙ לֹ֣א תִשְׁמָע֔וּהָ at oshb:Jer.13.17 (byte), whose second-person plural verb continues the plural audience addressed from 13:15.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: add the single variant note at oshb:Jer.13.16 with its type and single-witness disclosure alongside the paragraph marks already carried; add the flock lexeme crossing the row's closing seam from 13:17 to 13:20 with its swept object and verse count, stating why the cut still holds against it. strongest_rejected_alternative: re-ground the refusal of the lament typing on the span's bytes -- the plural address running through 13:17 -- rather than on which spans are enumerated. Test the cure must pass: every variant note falling inside the span appears in the row's disclosure set; every device straddling the row's own seams is disclosed with object and count; and no rejection rests on an enumeration in place of the span's bytes.

rulings.challenge_claim: Both challenges land on one ground: the rejection of the one-poem rival rests on reading 13:20 as addressed to a second-feminine-singular figure, on one of the twelve doubled-note verses of the variant inventory, with that doubled note undisclosed. One adds that the plural forms opening the verse contradict the reading and that two byte-true ties bracket the two-verse span undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: The same defect from both lenses, with a distinct second arm added by one of them; the defect is real and the stronger framing overstates it. oshb:Jer.13.20 carries two notes in the single-witness variant inventory -- a doubled-note verse -- and they sit on exactly the forms the rejection reads: the unpointed ketiv שאי and וראי stand in the verse bytes beside the pointed qere שְׂא֤וּ and וּרְא֔וּ (byte), whose plural endings are visible, and their object עֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ (byte) carries a second-person masculine plural suffix under either reading (that imperative-plus-object pair, sweep: 1 verse). The row asserts a second-feminine-singular addressee there and discloses no note, on the largest single-witness variant layer in the book. The characterization is right about the verse's second half -- לָ֔ךְ and תִּפְאַרְתֵּֽךְ (byte) are feminine singular -- and wrong about its opening, which is where the rejection places the shift. Second arm, byte-true and undisclosed: תִּֽפְאַרְתְּכֶֽם closes oshb:Jer.13.18 and recurs as תִּפְאַרְתֵּֽךְ at oshb:Jer.13.20 (that consonantal form, sweep: 4 verses, three of them in this chapter), and עֵ֥דֶר יְהוָֽה at oshb:Jer.13.17 recurs as הָעֵ֨דֶר֙ at oshb:Jer.13.20 (sweep: 6 verses) -- both tie this span to the material past its close and support the rival it sets aside. Framing correction: the seam is not falsified. The opening at oshb:Jer.13.18 is a morphological imperative, אֱמֹ֥ר לַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְלַגְּבִירָ֖ה (byte), naming a new addressee pair; the addressee does change at 13:20 under either reading of the doubled note; the paragraph disclosure for 13:18-19 is complete and correctly typed (setumah at MT 13:17 and MT 13:19, single-witness, tier-3) with no variant note inside the span; and the row already holds at reduced confidence with the frontier flag raised and concedes the rival's force. That places this at a ground-rewrite plus a mandatory disclosure, not at a falsified warrant.
rulings.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: re-ground the closing seam on what 13:20 actually carries -- plural imperatives with a second-person masculine plural object opening the verse, and the feminine-singular address governing from mid-verse -- instead of an unqualified second-feminine-singular characterization; the corrected ground must hold under BOTH the ketiv and the qere. device_notes: disclose the doubled variant note at oshb:Jer.13.20 with both members named and single-witness disclosure, and disclose the two ties crossing the row's edges -- the glory-crown form recurring from 13:18 at 13:20, and the flock lexeme recurring from 13:17 at 13:20 -- each with swept object and verse count, stating why the cut holds against them. Keep the row's reduced confidence and frontier flag. Test the cure must pass: no form-class ground stands on a verse carrying a variant note unless that note is disclosed and both members are read; and every device straddling the row's edges is disclosed with object and count.
